_readme: Copy of the defaults used to seed config/sources.json on first run. This file IS tracked in git; config/sources.json is NOT (see .gitignore) -- it holds machine-local paths and hostnames and is generated from this file automatically the first time the dashboard starts. Edit config/sources.json directly for your own machine; edit this file only if you want to change what a fresh install starts with. `refresh_preset` is 'normal' (the intervals_s below, unchanged) or 'relaxed' (roughly 3x longer -- for a laptop on battery); it is a multiplier over intervals_s, not a second set of numbers. `allow_config_writes` (default true) gates POST /api/config/layout and POST /api/config/theme -- the settings panel needs it true to save changes; set it false if you bind this dashboard beyond 127.0.0.1 (e.g. bind_host 0.0.0.0 on a LAN) and want it read-only from the browser. `disk_mounts` (default ["/"]) is the list of mounts the system panel reports on, local and remote; a mount that doesn't exist on a given host is skipped, not a failure. `collectors` (default {}, meaning auto-detect everything) lets you force a collector on or off regardless of auto-detection, e.g. {"beads": {"enabled": false}} -- a collector whose optional dependency (bd/~/.overlord/an ssh host) is absent starts inactive on its own and is re-checked every `collector_redetect_interval_s` seconds, so e.g. installing bd later brings its panel alive with no restart. `update_repo` defaults to "critfusion/critboard" -- that repo is public, so GET /api/update/check and the periodic background check (see `update_check_enabled` below) both work unauthenticated out of the box; POST /api/update/apply also requires allow_self_update: true. A fork should point this at its own "owner/repo". `update_check_enabled` (default true) turns on a background check every `update_check_interval_s` seconds (default 900); it is read-only (a conditional GET, ETag-cached, so a 15-minute poll costs nothing against GitHub's unauthenticated 60/hour limit) and safe with no other setting. `update_auto_apply` (default false) additionally lets that periodic check pull a fast-forward update on its own with no click, but only once allow_self_update is also true -- every existing apply_update safety check (clean tree, fast-forward only, configured origin only) still applies. GET/POST /api/settings/updates is the narrow settings-panel endpoint for these four (update_check_enabled, update_check_interval_s, allow_self_update, update_auto_apply): it never accepts arbitrary sources.json content. All four are toggles in the settings panel, so none of them need this file edited by hand; a hand edit here is picked up on the next settings read, without a restart. `bd_bin`/`herdr_bin` below are this repo's own dev host's paths -- install.sh resolves them for the machine it's actually installing on (PATH, then ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/local/bin, /usr/bin) and overwrites them in the freshly-generated config/sources.json, so these two values are placeholders, not a guarantee; run `make doctor` (or ./install.sh --doctor) any time to check every path this file has against what's actually on disk -- see INSTALL.md's "Tool & data path detection". `beads_env` is empty by default -- it is an optional, site-specific env file some `bd` setups source before every call (actor/DB config); a `bd` with its own local workspace (`bd init`, or `BEADS_DIR` set) needs no such file. Set it only if your setup actually uses one. `beads_dir` is empty by default -- set it to your beads workspace's `.beads` directory (NOT its parent) if the collector reports "no workspace configured" even though `bd` works fine from your own shell; install.sh tries to detect this automatically via `bd where --json`. It takes precedence over beads_env, which takes precedence over bd's own resolution. `bead_reply` (default `enabled: false`) turns on the bead popup's reply/send-back/close feature: `actor` is the BEADS_ACTOR a write runs as (empty = first entry of config/layout.json's human_labels, else "critboard-human"); `routes` is an ordered list of [substring, route_label] pairs matched case-insensitively against a bead's `created_by`, first match wins; `default_route` is used when nothing matches. Every write also requires `allow_config_writes` (above) to be true.
